name: Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation
text:
# Gradient Computation and Back-Propagation

Also called: Differentiable Rasterization Gradients, Back-Propagation in 3DGS

## Overview
This article defines the mathematical and algorithmic foundations for computing gradients of the loss function with respect to 3D Gaussian parameters during the training of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md). It addresses the problem of differentiating through the [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md), which is non-linear and order-dependent, to enable end-to-end optimization of Gaussian attributes. It sets apart from standard differentiable rendering by handling the specific opacity-transmittance coupling and recursive accumulation inherent to the Gaussian splatting rasterizer, extending to specialized variants for Time-of-Flight signals and [feature back-projection](#9769-gradient-weighted-feature-back-projection.md).

## Shared principles
The core mechanism relies on the chain rule applied to the [volume rendering integral](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md), discretized as a sum over sorted Gaussians. For a pixel, the rendered signal $S$ is computed via back-to-front accumulation. The gradient $\frac{\partial L}{\partial \theta_k}$ for a parameter $\theta_k$ of the $k$-th Gaussian depends on the gradient of the loss w.r.t. the final signal $\frac{\partial L}{\partial S}$ and the partial derivative of the signal w.r.t. the parameter.

The standard transmittance $T_k$ is defined as the product of non-opacities of all preceding Gaussians:
$$ T_k = \prod_{m < k} (1 - \alpha_m) $$
The rendered color $C$ is:
$$ C = \sum_{k} c_k \alpha_k T_k $$
The gradient of $C$ w.r.t. opacity $\alpha_k$ involves both the direct term and the indirect term through $T_j$ for $j > k$. In standard 3DGS, this results in a gradient proportional to $T_k(c_k - C_{accumulated})$.

For ToF signals, the accumulation model changes to include squared transmittance terms to account for non-linear intensity interactions, requiring modified recursive accumulators and gradient formulas.

For feature back-projection, the gradient of the rendered color w.r.t. the Gaussian color $\frac{\partial C}{\partial c_k} = \alpha_k T_k$ is used as a weighting factor to aggregate 2D features from training views into 3D Gaussians without iterative optimization.

## Subtopics

### [ToF Gradient Computation for Gaussian Splatting](9733-tof-gradient-computation-for-gaussian-splatting.md)
Computes gradients for Time-of-Flight image formation models. It extends the standard opacity gradient by introducing squared transmittance terms in the recursive accumulation, addressing the non-linear [interaction](#41-interaction.md) between opacity and ToF signal intensity. Choose this when optimizing Gaussian parameters against ToF quad pixel signals.

### [Gradient-Weighted Feature Back-Projection](9769-gradient-weighted-feature-back-projection.md)
A training-free method for rendering feature fields by aggregating 2D feature embeddings into 3D Gaussians. It uses the gradient of rendered color w.r.t. Gaussian color as a weight. Choose this for semantic segmentation or affordance transfer without the cost of training a separate feature field.

### [SNS Backward Pass with Intermediate Variable Q](10040-sns-backward-pass-with-intermediate-variable-q.md)
Introduces an intermediate variable $Q = ARS$ to decouple rotation $R$ and scale $S$ in gradient computation, avoiding complex coupling in the Jacobian. Choose this when optimizing rotation and scale parameters to simplify gradient derivation.

## Background
The gradient computation for 3D Gaussian Splatting is derived from the [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) framework. The standard back-propagation through the rasterizer was established in the [original 3DGS](#2805-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-software.md) paper [S1]. Extensions for ToF signals and feature fields have been developed to support specialized applications like depth estimation and semantic mapping.
